doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02

chapter: De De's career and trumpet players
title: De De's band travels: Paul Barnes, Nellie Lutcher, Texas, and sitting in with Bunk
summary: De De describes leaving with Paul Barnes and organizing a seven-piece band touring Louisiana and Texas, Nellie Lutcher as pianist, and sitting in with Bunk.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I'm telling you about myself. Well I left here with Paul Barnes. I think he's still playing. He's in Chicago now. He left here. Me and his brother. We formed a band and we traveled. Yeah, he was all signed. I got a card. Yeah, he got a card for him. And then we organized a seven piece band. Well then we traveled all around up to Lake Charles. There where we, Nellie Lutcher joined my band then. She was the pianist in our band. That's before I had married Willie, before I met Willie. And I traveled all over part of Texas, Louisiana, you know. They were with Paul.
Mm-hmm. Did you ever run across Lawrence Dewey out there in that part of the country around Lafayette or New Iberia?
I played all that way, in and out, you know. Let me see, Dewey. I'm trying to remember my name.
Clarinet player. Lawrence Dewey. What's his name? D-U-H-E. French scholar. Probably forgotten.
Probably I have. But some of the musicians I didn't meet, you know.
Did you ever play with the bunk at any time out there? No, no, I wouldn't say play. Set in, you know, on a job, you know.

Yeah. Yeah. Sometime he was in Iberville, I think. Iberville, Iberville, whatever you call it. And he was on the job and I'd go in there like fellas doing set in, you know. Yes. Few numbers like that before playing the job with him, no.
